headline: How an LLM Actually Works: Under the Hood
summary: Large Language Models are not sentient knowledge bases; they are statistical next-token prediction engines powered by vector geometry and self-attention. Understanding their internal data flow unlocks better architecture and low-latency system design.

slides.title: How an LLM Actually Works
slides.subtitle: Demystifying the high-dimensional mathematics behind modern generative AI.
slides.body: LLMs appear to think, but they simply calculate probabilities. Understanding their internal architecture transforms how you design AI systems.
slides.deep_dive: Under the hood, LLMs execute mathematical matrix transformations to predict the single most probable next token in sequence without maintaining long-term conscious state.
slides.key_fact: An LLM evaluates billions of parameters per forward pass to predict just one single token at a time.
slides.why_it_matters: Enables engineers to optimize prompt latency, memory bandwidth, and production model architectures.

slides.title: The Core Execution Pipeline
slides.subtitle: From raw human text to calculated token probabilities.
slides.body: Every LLM processes language through three distinct transformations: tokenization, attention scoring, and probability projection.

steps.title: Tokenization
steps.desc: Converts raw strings into discrete numerical IDs using predefined sub-word vocabularies.

steps.title: Vector Embedding
steps.desc: Maps token numbers into high-dimensional geometric coordinates that encode semantic relationships.

steps.title: Transformer Blocks
steps.desc: Runs multiple layers of self-attention and feed-forward networks to update contextual meanings.

steps.title: Softmax Head
steps.desc: Transforms final continuous vector states into a probability distribution over the entire vocabulary.

slides.title: Tokenization & Embeddings
slides.subtitle: Translating human vocabulary into mathematical geometry.
slides.body: Words become coordinates in space. Concepts with similar meanings sit closer together, allowing arithmetic operations on concepts.
slides.processing: The tokenizer slices words into IDs, while an embedding matrix assigns a high-dimensional vector with positional coordinates.
slides.output: A dense matrix of floating-point numbers ready for attention computation.

slides.title: The Self-Attention Engine
slides.subtitle: How words dynamically update their meaning based on surrounding context.
slides.body: Like spotlights on a stage, attention allows each word to inspect every other word to resolve ambiguity dynamically.

nodes.name: Queries (Q)
nodes.sub: What information is this word searching for?

nodes.name: Keys (K)
nodes.sub: What contextual cues does this word offer?

nodes.name: Values (V)
nodes.sub: What raw content does this word carry?

nodes.name: Attention Matrix
nodes.sub: Softmax weights routing focus across tokens

connections.label: Dot-product of Q and K computes relevance scores
Softmax normalizes relevance into focus percentages
Weights blend Value vectors into updated representations

slides.title: Training vs. Inference
slides.subtitle: Why training is compute-bound while real-time generation is memory-bound.
slides.body: Training processes thousands of tokens concurrently, while autoregressive generation is forced to run one serial step at a time.
left_items: Processes the entire context window simultaneously using causal masks.
Bottlenecked by tensor core arithmetic throughput and FLOPs.
Optimized for high batch throughput over single-token latency.
right_items: Generates tokens sequentially, requiring a complete forward pass per token.
Bottlenecked by memory bandwidth moving weights from VRAM to compute cores.
Requires KV-caching to prevent quadratic recalculation overhead.

slides.title: Treating LLMs as Databases
slides.subtitle: Confusing statistical word prediction with deterministic record lookups.
slides.body: LLMs approximate statistical associations, not factual tables. Forcing factual recall from weights leads directly to hallucinations.
slides.mistake_desc: Relying on internal parametric weights to store exact enterprise data, dynamic prices, or private records.
slides.solution_desc: Supplying verified facts in context, using the model purely as a reasoning and synthesis engine.

slides.title: Taming the Context Bottleneck
slides.subtitle: How production inference engines handle high-concurrency requests.
slides.body: Without caching, generating token 1,000 recalculates tokens 1 to 999 from scratch. KV-caching stores keys and values in GPU memory.
slides.scenario_context: Serving thousands of concurrent users with sub-second time-to-first-token requirements.
slides.scenario_solution: Inference runtimes allocate KV-cache like virtual memory pages, eliminating GPU memory fragmentation and multiplying concurrent serving capacity.

slides.title: System Design Summary
slides.subtitle: Foundational mental models for production AI architects.
slides.body: Master these structural mechanics to design cost-effective, low-latency applications on top of foundation models.
takeaways: LLMs are next-token predictors, not databases; use RAG for verified facts.
Self-attention scales quadratically; optimize context length to maintain latency.
Inference is memory-bandwidth bound; deploy KV-cache and quantization for throughput.
